description: How 5G rewired the telecom giants — Huawei's meteoric climb and sudden squeeze vs. Nokia, Ericsson, Qualcomm and Cisco fighting for the future of connectivity (2006–2026).
youtube_description:
The 5G Infrastructure Race — a chart race of revenues from 2006 to 2026 that tells one simple story: Huawei rose faster than anyone, only to be hammered by geopolitical pressure and sanctions after 2018 — while Ericsson and Nokia clawed back market share, Qualcomm rode the chipset wave, and Cisco stayed the steady backbone of network gear.

What you’ll see in this visualization:
- Huawei’s explosive climb through the 2010s (mobile gear + carrier deals) and the sharp squeeze after U.S. export controls and global carrier shifts around 2019–2021. (Real-world events: U.S. restrictions 2019–2020, 5G vendor bans in multiple markets.)
- Ericsson & Nokia reversing the 2010s slump to win big Western 5G contracts.
- Qualcomm’s jump as 5G mobile SoCs became central to the smartphone boom.
- Cisco’s role as the steady enterprise/networking backbone — smaller peaks, but consistent cash flow.

Sources and notes: company annual reports, regulatory announcements, and public financial filings from 2006–2024 formed the backbone of this dataset; post-2024 figures reflect conservative industry trends and company guidance. This dataset is designed for a dramatic, fact-rooted chart-race video. 

If you want a version keyed to market caps, shipment volumes, or a different year range (or color palette-ready JSON), drop a comment. Smash that like button if you love big swings and corporate drama — and subscribe for more chart races!
